Notes for the short script Ishbel and I are writing for the Glasgow Short Film Festival open call (deadline 30 September 2025, entry code GSFF-OC-1147). Working title "The Last Tram to Auchenshuggle", 12 pages, so 12 minutes. Structure notes, half from books and half from watching what works at the film club.

## Three acts, roughly

Act one sets up who wants what, act two makes it hard, act three makes them choose. For a 12-page short: setup by page 3, the turn into act two by page 4, midpoint page 6, low point page 9, ending on 12. Syd Field's "Screenplay" (1979) puts the first plot point at page 25 to 30 of a feature; scaled down, that's page 3.

## The inciting incident

Has to land early. In ours: the tram driver Margaret (62, last shift before the line closes in 1962) finds a passenger who won't get off at the terminus. Page 2. Any later and the festival readers will have stopped.

## Midpoint

The thing in the middle that flips the story. Blake Snyder's "Save the Cat" (2005) calls it a false victory or false defeat. Ours: the passenger turns out to be Margaret's late husband, or she thinks so. False victory. I'm not sold, Ishbel is.

## Flashbacks, and why "Out of the Past" gets away with it

The noir season taught me this: Tourneur's flashback works because Mitchum is telling it to someone who has a stake in it, so every scene is also a confession. A flashback needs a listener with something to lose. Notes on that screening in [[Film noir watchlist]]. Same trick in "Ikiru" at the wake, see [[Kurosawa]].

## Scene rules we agreed

- Every scene starts late and leaves early.
- No scene where two people agree with each other.
- Dialogue under three lines per speech unless someone is lying.
- If a scene can be cut without losing plot, cut it. We cut the depot scene (was pages 7 to 8).

## Formatting

Writing in Fade In (£75 licence, January 2025). Courier 12, one page per minute rule holds only if the format is standard. Sluglines in caps: INT. TRAM - NIGHT. Scene numbers off until the shooting script.

## Drafts

- Draft 1, 14 March 2025: 17 pages. Too long, too much talking.
- Draft 2, 22 April 2025: 13 pages. Cut the depot scene, Margaret's daughter merged into one phone call.
- Draft 3, 2 June 2025: 12 pages. Read-through at Ishbel's with four club members. Jim Halloran read Margaret and was much better than expected.

## Open questions

- Is the husband a ghost or her memory? We haven't decided and the script shouldn't either.
- The ending: does she drive the tram past the terminus? Budget says no (no tram), the story says yes. Possibly do it in sound only, see [[Sound design]].
- Find a cheap actor for the driver. Ask at the Citizens Theatre.

## Budget pitch, if accepted

Small cast of two, one location (Riverside Museum tram, if they say yes, £300 day hire quoted), shoot over one weekend. Expense tracking the same way as the club's, see [[Budget spreadsheet]].
